paper_title: Helioscope Bounds on Hidden Sector Photons
notes: Hidden (dark) photon kinetic mixing chi vs mass. Headline result is the Solar energy-loss / lifetime bound (abstract: chi <~ 1e-14), obtained by requiring the exotic hidden-photon luminosity be < L_sun = 3.83e26 W. Extracted the black "T-Lifetime" curve from Fig.6 (e-print vector file A2.pdf) via get_drawings; the paper states the L contribution (red L-Lifetime curve) does not change the limit appreciably, so T-Lifetime is the effective solar-lifetime bound. Calibration from axis tick strokes and label glyphs: x = Log10 m[eV] (-4 at x=48.4, 0 at 194.35), y = Log10 chi (-4 at y=36.5, -14 at y=307.1). Below ~1 eV the bound is a straight line of slope -2 (chi^2 m^4 flux); resonant production drives the minimum to chi~1.3e-14 near m~200-295 eV; beyond 295 eV it worsens (bulk emission), curve ends ~5e4 eV. chi reported directly (not chi^2). Curve clipped at the visible frame top (Log10 chi ~ -2.75); true bound continues to higher chi at lower mass off-plot. confidence_level is nominal: the energy-loss criterion is a luminosity bound, not a statistical CL. The separate CAST helioscope curve (blue) is a distinct, generally weaker recast and was not selected. No dark-matter density dependence (solar production).
